films.title: Desert One
films.synopsis:
DESERT ONE uniquely blends emotion and bravado to tell the incredible tale of America’s secret mission to free the hostages of the 1979 Iranian revolution. Kopple discovers a wealth of unearthed archival sources and receives unprecedented access, engaging in intimate conversations with many of the soldiers closest to the story, some for the first time, as well as President Jimmy Carter, Vice President Walter Mondale and TV newsman Ted Koppel. Evocative new animation brings audiences closer than anyone has ever gotten to being on the inside for this history-making operation.

At a moment when tensions once again rise between the governments of Iran and the U.S., old wounds remain painfully current for many on each side who detail their recollections in DESERT ONE -- but talk of hope also emerges, that the lessons of the past might finally guide us to a better future.
films.after_screening: Post-screening discussion to follow with director Barbara Kopple and film subjects: David Aaron - Carter Administration; Kevin Hermening - Hostage, U.S. Embassy Marine Guard; Captain Wade Ishimoto - U.S. Army, Delta Force; John Limbert - Hostage, U.S. Foreign Services; Michael Metrinko - Hostage, U.S. Foreign Services; Gerald Rafshoon - Carter Administration; Major James Q. Roberts - U.S. Army; Colonel Ed Seiffert - U.S. Marine Corps; Cyntia Seiffert

films.title: The Preppy Murder: Death in Central Park
films.synopsis: A five-part investigative documentary that revisits the infamous murder of Jennifer Levin at the hands of her prep school friend Robert Chambers in Central Park in the summer of 1986. The case became a tabloid sensation and sparked a national conversation on female sexuality, power and privilege. Award winning filmmakers Ricki Stern and Annie Sundberg take a fresh look at the case, meticulously blending a trove of archival material with contemporary interviews, in a retrospective glance marked by haunting new perspective on the case that shook a city, if not a nation.
films.after_screening: The first two installments of the series will be prefaced with an introduction by the filmmakers

films.title: Citizen K
films.synopsis: Academy Award winning filmmaker Alex Gibney’s revelatory CITIZEN K is an intimate yet sweeping look at post-Soviet Russia from the perspective of the enigmatic Mikhail Khodorkovsky, a former oligarch turned political dissident. Benefitting from the chaos that ensued after the dissolution of the U.S.S.R., Khodorkovsky managed to amass a fortune in financing and oil production and became the richest man in Russia. Until he accused the new Putin regime of corruption. Khodorkovsky was arrested, his assets seized. Following a series of show trials, he was sentenced to more than ten years in prison. Today, as an exile living in London, he continues to denounce Putin’s two-decade stranglehold on power. Expertly researched and photographed, Gibney uses Khodorkovsky’s story as a way to explore the complex interplay between oligarchy and government and its destructive effect on democracy, in Russia and beyond.
films.after_screening: Post-screening discussion to follow with director

films.title: Bellingcat: Truth in a Post-Truth World
films.synopsis: The film follows the revolutionary rise of the controversial “citizen investigative journalist” collective known as Bellingcat, a group of online researchers dedicated to exposing the truth of impenetrable news stories from around the world. Bellingcat’s impact is examined through the lens of its current investigations, as well as the high-profile conflicts the group has previously reported. With governments growing less reliable by the day and traditional newspapers declining in relevance and reach – how does Bellingcat, dismissed by some critics as an assortment of “armchair researchers”, attain such a prominent status in the new world order of news? The filmmaker takes us on a quest to understand the group’s innovations, challenging our concept of journalism.
films.after_screening: Post-screening conversation to follow with film subjects Christiaan Triebert and Claire Wardle

films.title: Bully. Coward. Victim. The Story of Roy Cohn
films.synopsis:
Legendary and controversial attorney Roy Cohn was a power broker in the rough and tumble world of New York City business and politics. Senator Joseph R. McCarthy’s top counsel during investigations into Communist activities in the 1950s, Cohn is also known for being Donald Trump’s former personal lawyer, fixer and mentor.

Focusing on key periods of his life, and drawing on extensive, newly unearthed archival material, director Ivy Meeropol examines the man who has both repelled and fascinated her for much of her life. Cohn, who prosecuted her grandparents, Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, in what became known as the “atomic spies” case; obtained their convictions in court and then insisted on their executions.
films.after_screening: Post-screening discussion to follow with director

films.title: In Dry Water
films.synopsis: Adama and Adja have a problem on their hands. Their country, Senegal, is running out of fish. As foreign trawlers and climate change cripple their stocks, the friends face a choice: Stay or follow the same trail as the fish.

films.title: Waiting for Tearah
films.synopsis: An intimate portrait of a mother struggling to find mental health care for her child. Shot over two years, this verité film tells the story of Shayna, a single parent of three girls on the brink of losing her home due to medical costs, while her eldest daughter, Tearah, waits for months in a psychiatric hospital. Day after day, Shayna navigates a complicated maze of government agencies as she fights for much-needed treatment for Tearah. Above all, Waiting for Tearah is about a mother’s love, and her unwillingness to give up on her daughter.

films.title: Poppy Crash
films.synopsis: As addiction to the opioid fentanyl surges in the U.S., causing an unprecedented number of overdoses, violence spikes in the mountains of Guerrero, Mexico. Fentanyl is cheaper and more potent, which has slashed natural opium prices, leaving the indigenous poppy farmers in Guerrero with few options for survival. Poppy Crash chronicles the stories of three indigenous farmers who worked in the opium harvest since they were children and suddenly had their livelihood ripped out from under them. Gustavo attempted to migrate to the U.S., and following his deportation, he joined the rank and file of a local crime group and now works as a hitman. Gutierrez substituted poppy with corn, but with a 90% cut in profits, he can’t make ends meet. Yulis, a young mother, traveled thousands of miles from home, leaving her two young children behind to work as a migrant farmworker, but suffered from wage theft. Their dependence on the international drug economy and the volatile market has left these communities with an uncertain future where increased poverty and violence is evident.
films.after_screening: Post-screening discussion to follow with filmmakers

films.title: The Cave
films.synopsis: Oscar nominee Feras Fayyad (LAST MAN IN ALEPPO) delivers an unflinching story of the Syrian war with his powerful new documentary, The Cave. For besieged civilians, hope and safety lie underground inside the subterranean hospital known as the Cave, where pediatrician and managing physician Dr. Amani Ballour and her colleagues Samaher and Dr. Alaa have claimed their right to work as equals alongside their male counterparts, doing their jobs in a way thatwould be unthinkable in the oppressively patriarchal culture that exists above. Following the women as they contend with daily bombardments, chronic supply shortages and the ever-present threat of chemical attacks, The Cave paints a stirring portrait of courage, resilience and female solidarity.
films.after_screening: A post screening discussion will follow with director, Feras Fayyad

films.title: Lost and Found
films.synopsis: Separating thousands of families from loved ones along the way, a campaign of ethnic cleansing and violence perpetrated by the Myanmar military has driven more than 700,000 Rohingya from their homes. LOST AND FOUND, directed by Orlando von Einsiedel, is the story of Kamal Hussein, a Rohingya refugee who has dedicated his life to reuniting children with their parents.

films.title: Refuge(e)
films.synopsis: REFUGE(E) traces the incredible journey of two refugees, Alpha and Zeferino. They each fled violent threats to their lives in their home countries and presented themselves at the US border asking for political asylum, only to be incarcerated in for-profit prison for months on end without having committed any crime. They represent thousands more like them who can’t tell their stories.

films.title: The Nightcrawlers
films.synopsis: An unflinching, verité-style exposé, THE NIGHTCRAWLERS follows a determined group of photojournalists on their mission to chronicle the deadly battle being waged against the Philippines’ drug epidemic — and the tragic cost of this brutal crusade. Directed with pulse-pounding intensity by first-time director Alexander A. Mora, the documentary trails Raffy Lerma, a former staff photographer for a prominent newspaper, as he joins forces with a team of bold freelance photojournalists, or “nightcrawlers,” who are covering a wave of extrajudicial killings that, by some estimates, has claimed as many as 27,000 lives. With unprecedented access, the film also features shocking interviews with members of a mysterious death squad that prowls the city’s back alleys in search of people they are paid to kill with impunity.
films.after_screening: Post-screening discussion to follow with filmmakers

films.title: Dark Suns
films.synopsis: An unforgettable epic, running two-and-a-half hours and offering harrowing yet utterly urgent testimony from the friends and families of those who vanished. DARK SUNS chronicles the hundreds of murders of women, journalists, students, and activists in Mexico since the 1990s, and the insidious culture of cartel violence and state corruption behind them. Spanning the notorious femicides in Ciudad Juárez at the northern border to the murders of journalists in Veracruz in the south, director Julien Elie draws on the testimony of determined investigators, family members, journalists, priests, lawyers, and activists, tracing a path of organized and unpunished criminality that involves drug and human trafficking, extortion, kidnapping, and collusion with the governments on both sides of the border.
films.after_screening: Post-screening discussion to follow with journalist Ricardo Sandoval Palos

films.title: Bedlam
films.synopsis: Through intimate stories of patients, families, and medical providers, BEDLAM immerses us in the national crisis surrounding care of the severely mentally ill. Filmed over five years, BEDLAM brings us inside one of America’s busiest psychiatric emergency rooms, into jails where psychiatric patients are warehoused, and to the homes – and homeless encampments – of mentally ill members of our communities, where silence and shame often compound personal suffering. The story is told in part by director Kenneth Paul Rosenberg, MD, whose own life journey has been profoundly impacted by a severely mentally ill family member.
films.after_screening: Post-screening discussion to follow with director

films.title: Bikram: Yogi, Guru, Predator
films.synopsis: BIKRAM: YOGI, GURU, PREDATOR examines the dramatic rise and fall of the controversial founder of hot yoga, Bikram Choudhury. Arriving in Beverly Hills from Calcutta, India in the early 1970s, Choudhury quickly cultivated a celebrity following and built a global fitness empire that furnished him with extreme wealth. But by the 2010s, as numerous sexual abuse allegations emerged and stories of his aggressive, cult-like training environment surfaced, the lawsuits started to mount and Choudhury’s unorthodox teaching style became front-page news. Directed by Academy Award winner Eva Orner (Taxi to the Dark Side, Chasing Asylum) and produced by Sarah Anthony (The Price of Free, The Defiant Ones), BIKRAM: YOGI, GURU, PREDATOR shines a light on the stories of the women who took him down and explores the contradiction of how this healing discipline could simultaneously help and hurt so many.
films.after_screening: Post-screening discussion to follow with Julia Lowrie Henderson, creator of ESPN Bikram podcast

sessions.title: Opening Conversation: Race in Focus
sessions.description: The fifth edition of DX kicks off with a timely conversation, featuring Wesley Lowery, a Pulitzer-Prize winning national reporter for the Washington Post covering law enforcement, justice, race and politics, and, multi-award winning documentary filmmakers Marco Williams and Michèle Stephenson. Together, they will examine the representation of race and the black experience through film and journalism. As new scholarship arising from the 400th anniversary of 1619 — when the first pirate ship delivered more than 20 African captives to the Virginia shore — suggests, the legacy of bondage and racial subjugation shapes nearly every aspect of modern life, from labor relations to law, from education to the economy, from art to ethics, and much more. Investigative storytellers in print and film are challenging the white gaze and its underlying presumptions, bringing new questions and lines of investigation to the stories of our times.

sessions.title: Investigative Podcasts: The Sound and the Fury
sessions.description: It’s been five years since the investigative podcast that started it all, Serial, emerged on the scene, and since then the format has exploded with some of the most captivating investigative storytelling to be found in any medium. Hear from creators and producers of some of the very best in audio investigations today, from West Cork, named after the quaint Irish region that became the unlikely backdrop to the 1996 murder of Sophie Toscan du Plantier, a French film producer, to the multi-season In the Dark which examines in electrifying and infuriating detail a child-abduction in season one and a wrongful imprisonment in season two, and reveals the inner machinations of the investigative process as much as a judicial system gone awry. And finally, Dr. Death, which examines charismatic neurosurgeon Christopher Duntsch who was convicted of gross malpractice after thirty-one of his patients were left seriously injured after he operated on them, and two patients died during his operation.

sessions.title: When No One Else Is Watching
sessions.description: Before the public sets eyes on many of the most compelling investigative works, journalists, filmmakers, and even human rights advocates encounter myriad ethical questions along the way. Speakers on this panel are immortalizing people in crisis, sometimes at their most vulnerable: in the immediate aftermath of mass violence (as in Emily Taguchi’s AFTER PARKLAND), or in the throes of acute bodily trauma (such as Luke Lorentzen’s MIDNIGHT FAMILY) or, in the case of the advocacy group Witness, filming victims of human rights abuses in order to further public engagement, policy change, and justice. We’ll unpack the moral issues involved, as filmmakers and advocates grapple with subjects at their most fragile and exposed. What does a filmmaker reveal? What is left off-screen? What is the moral compass that guides their encounters with vulnerable subjects, and how does this shape their storytelling decisions “when no one else is watching,” to cite author and philosopher Aldo Leopold.

sessions.title: The Visual Newsroom
sessions.description: Newsrooms are increasingly turning toward film as an essential medium for opening new dimensions in storytelling, unpacking investigations, and reaching different audiences. We’ll hear from newsrooms at the forefront of this shift.

sessions.title: The Undertow
sessions.description: Filmmakers and journalists working in the investigative mode often face great risks — personally, legally, monetarily, even bodily — to expose hidden corruption or bring clarity to a profoundly complex issue. Largely, the threats remain invisible to audiences and readers. The full influence of threat and danger, however, often go beyond the concrete steps practitioners take to work safely and reduce risk. Danger can also shape the investigative process, impinge on the storytelling that results, and continue to stalk sources and subjects, long after the credits have rolled. Nanfu Wang’s (HOOLIGAN SPARROW) newest film, ONE CHILD NATION, explores the profound effects of government policy on generations of Chinese parents and children. Ramona Diaz, who may be best known for her compelling character-driven documentaries, most notably of Philippine first lady Imelda Marcos, is now at work on a new film examining disinformation. Andalusia Knoll Soloff, a multimedia journalist based in Mexico City, traces the opioid epidemic in the U.S. to the poppy fields in Mexico, and trains her lens on the fragile ecosystem between migrant farmers, local drug lords, and the great consumer up north.

sessions.title: DX Access / Pitch
sessions.description:
Thursday, October 10 & Friday October 11.

DX ACCESS connects registered attendees to representatives of the most respected and innovative organizations and individuals in film and journalism, and provides unparalleled face time with funders, producers, festival programmers, distributors, media outlets, reporters, writers and directors. In pre-arranged one-on-one meetings, industry leaders unpack how they work, learn more about projects, either planned or in progress, with a view to exploring the potential for collaboration or support.

Through DX PITCH, journalists and filmmakers pitch their ideas for investigative projects to the programmers and editors of award-winning and innovative platforms. In face-to-face pitch sessions, accepted applicants have the opportunity to make a verbal pitch, receive feedback, and learn about real opportunities for distribution on prestigious national platforms.

Through DX ACCESS and DX PITCH, registered participants in Double Exposure have found funding for projects, distribution deals, new homes for thier work and jobs.

sessions.title: #MeToo 2.0
sessions.description: The calling out of sexual predators, that began with women in the film industry unmasking Harvey Weinstein, has deepened and grown. Hear from journalists at the Miami Herald, whose dogged reporting forced prosecutors to reopen the Jeffrey Epstein case, and from the filmmakers behind “Surviving Jeffrey Epstein,” a new multi-part documentary from Lifetime (which borrows its nomenclature from Lifetime’s breakthrough multi-part documentary Surviving R. Kelly). This panel will examine the heroic efforts and scrupulous methods undertaken by investigative journalists and filmmakers to render visible, through print and film, predators “hiding in plain sight.”

sessions.title: Docs in Progress Pitch
sessions.description:
Six projects originally presented by documentary organizations Docs In Progress and The D-Word at Peer Pitch programs in four regions of the country have been selected to return to Washington DC for an industry pitch at the Double Exposure Investigative Film Festival fifth addition. The pitching filmmakers present their projects to a panel that includes representatives from across the documentary industry.

PITCH PROJECTS:

Buying Time (Sara Barger – Washington DC)

As a Virginia family faces their 10-year old daughter’s brain cancer, they are doing everything they can do to keep her alive and alleviate her pain, including breaking federal laws by buying cannabis products and having them shipped across state lines.

Dark Summit (Amy Marquis – Boulder, CO)

Mefloquine is an anti-malarial drug with side effects — ranging from anxiety and hallucinations to suicide and homicidal rage — that have affected millions of injured soldiers, diplomats, and civilians. This is a global crisis, but for the filmmaker, it’s also personal: Her life partner was among the first American civilians to take the drug in 1992, and it’s affected every moment of his life since.

The Long Rescue (Jennifer Huang – Oakland, CA)

Hope, Sara, and Carrie come of age in a clandestine shelter for survivors of child sex trafficking in Cebu, Philippines. We follow them over five years as they rebuild their lives and re-enter the world, only to confront the same poverty, predators, and pimps of their childhood.

Norteños (Rodrigo Dorfman and Peter Eversoll – Durham, NC)

After decades of living as immigrants in the United States, several “Norteños” return to their hometown in rural Michoacan, Mexico, bringing a piece of the good old USA back with them. This is an unfiltered and nuanced portrait of the people redefining the boundaries of a new Global South through their experiences in el Norte.

Queer (Cai Thomas – Chicago, IL and Serena Ajbani – Washington DC)

This interactive documentary series is a community-led documentary walking tour outlining the personal and collective queer histories as they relate to place. The stories include an urban planner and choreographer in Los Angeles who first understood his queerness through experiences on public transportation; a Black trans actor who found self-acceptance in her life shaped by community spaces in New Orleans; and a two-spirited person in the Kanien’kéha:ka Territory where Tio:tia’ke/Montreal is located, complicating the notion of queer belonging on stolen land.

Undue Burdens (Andrea Raby – Chicago, IL)

In many midwestern states, TRAP laws force women seeking abortions to travel hundreds of miles to the nearest clinic and face waiting periods, meaning many women struggle to afford the time and expense involved in accessing the procedure. That’s where practical abortion funds like Midwest Access Coalition come in. They are following in the footsteps of organizations like Jane that provided access to abortions prior to Roe v. Wade.

sessions.title: Age of Consent
sessions.description: Inherent in the role of journalist or filmmaker is the desire to tell a story, often toward a greater good. Whether with notebook or camera lens, the storyteller is framing the investigation, sometimes spending long years immersed in a place or situation, sometimes parachuting in. Increasingly, however, subjects are questioning the authority of outsiders to tell their stories. They are demanding a say over how they are represented and objecting when they are not consulted. Foundations are taking notice, and developing policies to promote community involvement in the creative or reporting process. This shift marks a departure from, and challenge to, the traditional journalistic stance of the neutral investigator.

sessions.title: The New Transparency
sessions.description: For most of the last hundred years, trust resided in a name: of a reporter, of a news outlet, of a filmmaker or a studio. As New York University professor Jay Rosen has noted, that’s changing fast. In an age of widespread public mistrust of media and organized disinformation, the ability of readers and audiences to understand, and verify, the news gathering process has become key to credibility, replacing reputation the barometer of trust. That means disclosing the assumptions and biases of journalists and filmmakers, unpacking the steps of an investigation and choices along the way and, even, welcoming non-journalists into the reporting process. Activists are showing readers and viewers how to cross-check information, how to mine social media and open source data, and how to trace the provenance of questionable images and information. Their goal: to produce more reliable and trustworthy stories, and more savvy consumers of media.

sessions.title: Ask Me Anything: Meet the Funders
sessions.description: Everything you always wanted to know from funders but were afraid to ask. We’ll be collecting anonymous questions from festival attendees and posing them to the assembled funders, who have promised to answer whatever’s on your mind, no holds barred. Bring it on . . .

sessions.title: The Big Chill
sessions.description: The stakes are rising for whistleblowers across the globe. In the United States, whistleblowers are facing prosecution under the Espionage Act like never before, a charge that carries a potential life sentence for speaking up to expose wrongdoing. Elsewhere, whistleblowers face financial and professional ruin, smear campaigns and–in some countries–targeted assassination. What does this mean for the watchdogs in print and film?

sessions.title: FOIA Workshop for Journalists and Filmmakers
sessions.description: Federal, state, and local governments possess a wealth of information that can be of great use to journalists, including documentary filmmakers, but obtaining that material under state and federal public records laws isn’t always easy. This workshop led by media attorneys from the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press will help you learn how to successfully navigate FOI laws, from crafting strong public records requests to overcoming denials. Presented in collaboration with The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, International Documentary Association, and the Hollywood Foreign Press Association.

sessions.title: Open Source Investigations and Verification
sessions.description: Publically available tools now make it possible for citizens and independent journalists to investigate and verify content. In this hands-on workshop, you will learn how to channel your inner Sherlock Holmes and use open source tools to verify content.

sessions.title: Pro Bono Legal Clinic
sessions.description: The Pro Bono Legal Clinic offers investigative storytellers lacking legal representation the opportunity to connect with experts who can knowledgeably discuss legal challenges they are confronting. Leading attorneys in the areas First Amendment law, privacy and libel, Freedom of Information, whistleblower protection, copyright and intellectual property will be on hand. Attorneys will brief participants on case law and trends relevant to the problems that journalists and filmmakers have articulated upon registering for the clinic, and field questions from them. Attorneys have also agreed to consider representing select participants in need of counsel on an ongoing basis pro bono. All Access pass holders receive a link via email to pre-register for the Legal Clinic. They should describe the legal challenges they are facing to ensure participating attorneys are aware of their issues.

sessions.title: Crossing Borders
sessions.description:
A new initiative of Double Exposure 2019, Crossing Borders brings representatives from film programming organizations and journalistic organizations together to give feedback on select projects in front of a live audience. Newsrooms moving print projects into film, and filmmakers venturing into investigative territory, show excerpts of their work and receive feedback from across the aisle. The goal for each side is to raise impact through input from colleagues drawing on unaccustomed expertise. In practice, this means traditionally text-based news operations will hear directly from film programmers about how to strengthen the visual story they are telling. Filmmakers who may lack a background in journalism can learn more about using journalism to undergird character-driven stories and connect them to the broader issues at stake.

Projects being presented:

MARTHA, A film by Anne Alvergue and Debra McClutchy

She was once as famous as Jackie O. And then she tried to take down a President. Martha is a portrait of the unlikeliest of whistleblowers: Martha Mitchell, a Republican cabinet wife who was gas-lighted by the Nixon Administration to keep her quiet. It offers a female gaze on Watergate through the voice of the woman herself.

A BROKEN TRUST, A film by Maren Machles and Carrie Cochran

There’s a place in America where the criminal justice system can legally discriminate. For Indigenous sexual assault survivors on tribal lands, their legal status as an “Indian” sends their case through an entirely different criminal justice system. And in some tribal communities, there’s a common belief here that it’s not if you will be assaulted, but when. This story is a rare glimpse into a severely stressed and complex system and the lives of the people who work within it, trying to make their communities better.

DEEPSIDE A film by Jason Fitzroy Jeffers and Jess Swanson

An independent investigation into the drowning of a Broward county teenager raises questions about the conduct and reporting of the police and medical examiner’s office.
